subject: POC onboarding: traffic & success criteria (FinVista)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finvista.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC onboarding: traffic & success criteria (FinVista)

Thanks again for the call this morning, Daniel — good alignment across scope and timelines. This thread is a quick written recap and a proposed next-step plan so we can lock in the POC kickoff next week.

Key takeaways from our call:
- Objective: 3-week POC to validate inference latency, throughput, and cost for FinVista's API-driven chat assistant. Primary success measure is meeting 95th pct latency < 300ms at steady-state traffic and handling peak bursts without >1% error rate.
- Integrations: your team will route traffic to a Redwood test endpoint (staging API key) behind a feature flag.
- Data: No customer PII in test traffic; all production-like prompts redacted per our conversation.

Traffic intake (please confirm / correct):
- Steady RPS: 6–12 requests/sec (mixed chat and single-turn generate)
- Peak bursts: up to 120 RPS for short bursts (90–180s), expected 1–2x per day during batch jobs
- Concurrency: 12–20 concurrent connections from multiple processes
- Token profile: mean input ~80 tokens, mean output ~120 tokens, 95th token length ~420 tokens, absolute max ~512 tokens
- Endpoint mix: ~70% chat (chat-complete), ~30% single-shot generation (summarize/plain_generate)
- Auth & headers: you’ll send X-Correlation-ID header; we’ll ingest for tracing

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) Kickoff & environment handoff (Day 0): share staging API key, test endpoints, and workbook (attached). Owner: Soojin (sales) / Marcus (SE)
2) Smoke test (Day 1–2): validate connectivity and a small sample of 200 requests; confirm latency baseline
3) Load run (Day 3–7): run steady-state and scheduled burst tests; capture token-level telemetry
4) Evaluation & readout (Day 15): compare against success criteria and recommend runtime profile

Success criteria (proposed):
- 95th percentile latency < 300ms for chat at steady RPS
- Error rate < 1% during peak bursts (observability on retries/timeouts)
- Average per-token cost within the estimate we discussed (we'll model cost after first 24h of traffic)
- No security/compliance blockers for Private deployment (if required)

Immediate asks for you before kickoff:
- Confirm or correct the traffic numbers above
- Provide any redaction rules you use (we can add a small transform on our side if needed)
- Confirm preferred kickoff date (we suggested Aug 18 or 19)

Attachments: poc-workbook.xlsx (handbook + telemetry fields + sample payloads)

Thanks — I’ll loop Marcus in for the technical runbook once you confirm the numbers.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finvista.ai>

Subject: Re: POC onboarding: traffic & success criteria (FinVista)

Thanks, Soojin — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and answers below.

Confirmed traffic profile (FYI):
- Steady RPS: baseline 8 rps; during business hours 10–12 rps
- Peak bursts: historically we see a ~2–3 minute spike up to 120 RPS during digest runs; occasional long bursts up to ~250 RPS but those are rare (we can schedule a controlled run)
- Concurrency: our API layer uses 16 pooled connections to the model infra
- Token profile: mean input 75–90 tokens, outputs typically 60–160 tokens; we do have a few heavier prompts that hit ~500 tokens
- Mix: ~60% chat-style multi-turn, ~40% single-shot summarization/generation

Notes & asks from our side:
- We need to verify how Redwood handles long KV cache warmups across conversation contexts — Marcus please advise on warmup strategy.
- Can you provide a short test harness script (curl/node) that mimics our headers and token lengths?
- Security: we'll need your SOC2 attestation and an outline of data retention controls before we send any production-like traces (sending to Ayesha to coordinate).

Kickoff: Aug 19 works better for our engineering lead. Can we aim for 9am PT?

Thanks,
Daniel
Director of Platform Engineering, FinVista
Daniel.Park@finvista.ai | +1 617-555-1089

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finvista.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC onboarding: traffic & success criteria (FinVista)

Thanks for the details, Daniel — helpful. Quick tech notes and a minimal action list from SE side.

Technical clarifications we recommend for the POC:
- KV cache / warmup: for multi-turn chat we'll use session-scoped KV caching. Expect 1–2 warmup tokens per conversation; recommend running a 15-minute ramp where we replay recent contexts so the cache stabilizes ahead of the main burst.
- Batching & chunking: we'll test continuous batching with max batch window 20ms initially; if latency is above target we'll reduce batching and bump up concurrency.
- Quantization / model variant: we'll bring a 4-bit quantized variant for cost-sensitive runs and a full FP16 variant for latency-sensitive checks. We'll run both and present a cost/latency tradeoff.
- Telemetry: please include X-Correlation-ID and conversation-id headers; we will return X-Redwood-Trace with each response. We'll need a sample of 500 unique request IDs for complete trace coverage.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marcus: deliver test harness (node + curl) and the SE runbook (attached) by EOD Aug 17 — attachment: traffic-acceptance-checklist.md
- Ayesha: share SOC2 link and redaction rules before Aug 18
- Soojin: send staging API key + kickoff invite for Aug 19 09:00 PT

Run plan: during the load window we propose three phases: 1) steady run at 10 rps for 4 hours, 2) scheduled bursts (3x 120–150 rps for 3 minutes each), 3) one stress run to 250 rps for 60s (controlled). We'll capture latency curves, retry rates, and token cost.

Link to SE notebook and runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abcd1234

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
